title: month
summary: Extract month components from datetime values in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Documented datetime and legacy serial/text inputs execute on the host. RunMat-only resident inputs gather through their owning provider after compatibility admission.

description: `month(t)` extracts calendar-month values from datetime input. Datetime input supports `monthofyear`, `name`, and `shortname`; documented legacy serial-number and date-text forms support an optional input format.
behaviors: `month(t)` accepts datetime scalars and datetime arrays.
The output shape matches the input shape.
Month values use the standard 1-through-12 numbering.
`month(t,'name')` and `month(t,'shortname')` return shaped cells of character month names for datetime input.
Documented legacy binary64 serial date numbers and date text return double month numbers with matching shape.
Single-precision and all eight typed-integer legacy serial inputs are a gated RunMat extension; exact native values are range-checked before one binary64 serial-date conversion.

Extract months from a datetime array

faqs.question: What numbering does `month` use?
faqs.answer: It returns January as `1` through December as `12`.

faqs.question: Does `month` preserve the input shape?
faqs.answer: Yes. The numeric output has the same size as the input datetime array.

faqs.question: Does `month` run on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. datetime values are host-side objects, so `month` executes on the CPU.

gpu_residency: Documented `month` forms are host-side. RunMat can admit resident legacy numeric input as an extension, gathers it non-destructively through the exact owner, and returns the documented host result.
gpu_behavior: `month` does not dispatch a GPU kernel. Explicit resident input is a separately gated RunMat extension, while internal automatic residency can gather transparently.
